examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 변장하고 도시를 돌아다녀요.
examples.en: The main character in the movie walks around the city in disguise.
A disguised police officer waited for the criminal at the market.
I dressed up as a witch for Halloween.
Even with sunglasses and a hat as a disguise, I recognized the person right away.
The children dressed up as animals and took photos.
The disguise was so perfect that nobody knew.

explain: '변장'은 다른 사람인 척하려고 옷이나 겉모습을 바꾸는 일이에요. '분장'은 연극이나 영화처럼 역할을 위해 꾸미는 거라서 다르고, '변장'은 정체를 숨기거나 속일 때 써요. 보통 '변장하다'로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: He disguised himself as an old man.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변장'을 동사로 쓴 말이에요. '~으로 변장하다'로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, often used as '~으로 변장하다' (disguise as ~).

phrases.en: After the job was done, he took off his disguise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바꾼 모습을 원래대로 돌릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for removing a disguise and going back to one's normal look.

phrases.example: 변장한 모습을 보고 아무도 못 알아봤어요.
phrases.en: No one recognized him when they saw him in disguise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변장한 상태를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the disguised look of someone.

explain_en: Deliberately changing appearance, as in costume or to hide identity. '변장' means changing your clothes or look to pass as someone else. '분장' is made up for a role, as in a play or film, while '변장' is for hiding or deceiving about identity. It is mostly used as the verb '변장하다'.

t90.ax: I dressed up as a witch for Halloween.

examples.ko: 작은 실수가 큰 싸움의 빌미가 됐어요.
examples.en: A small mistake became the cause of a big fight.
That one remark was what set off the misunderstanding.
Be careful not to give the other side an opening to use against you.

examples.ko: 회사는 그 사고를 빌미로 직원 교육을 강화했어요.
examples.en: The company used that accident as a pretext to strengthen employee training.

examples.ko: 그는 병을 빌미 삼아 모임에 나오지 않았어요.
examples.en: He used his illness as an excuse not to come to the gathering.
No one knows who gave the cause for it.

explain: 대개 좋지 않은 일의 원인이나 핑계로 나와요. '빌미가 되다', '빌미를 주다', '빌미로 삼다'처럼 굳은 표현으로 많이 써요. 좋은 일의 원인에는 잘 안 쓰고, 그럴 땐 '계기'를 써요.

phrases.en: By breaking the promise, I gave the other person a pretext.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이나 불평이 생길 원인을 만들어 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means creating a cause for trouble or complaints.

phrases.example: 그는 작은 실수를 빌미로 삼아 화를 냈어요.
phrases.en: He used a small mistake as an excuse to get angry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 핑계 삼아 다른 행동을 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means using something as a pretext to do something else.

phrases.en: Saying you were busy is just an excuse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빌미보다 쉬운 말로, 일상에서 변명할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word than 빌미, commonly used for excuses in daily life.

explain_en: A pretext one seizes on to blame or start trouble. It usually refers to the cause of, or an excuse for, something bad. It is mostly used in fixed phrases like 빌미가 되다, 빌미를 주다, and 빌미로 삼다. For the cause of something good, people say 계기 instead.

examples.ko: 이 사건이 두 사람이 멀어진 시발점이었어요.
examples.en: This incident was the starting point of the two growing apart.
Seoul Station is the starting point of this line.

examples.ko: 작은 오해가 큰 싸움의 시발점이 됐어요.
examples.en: A small misunderstanding became the start of a big fight.
It takes about an hour from the starting point to the terminus.

examples.ko: 시발점에서 버스를 타면 앉아서 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you board the bus at the starting point, you can sit down.
I still don't know what the starting point of the change was.

explain: 버스나 지하철이 출발하는 곳, 그리고 어떤 일이 시작된 계기를 말할 때 써요. '출발점'은 더 넓게 쓰이고, 시발점은 노선의 시작이나 일이 커진 계기를 말할 때 자주 들려요. 반대말은 '종점'이에요.

phrases.example: 그 책 한 권이 제 꿈의 시발점이 됐어요.
phrases.en: That one book became the starting point of my dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 시작된 계기를 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form for the trigger that started something.

phrases.en: Where is the starting point of this bus?
phrases.nuance_ko: 노선이 출발하는 곳을 가리킬 때 쓰고, 반대는 '종점'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to where a route begins; the opposite is 종점 (terminus).

phrases.en: This is the starting point of our trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시발점보다 넓게 쓰고 일상 대화에서도 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 시발점 and natural in everyday speech.

explain_en: Where a big change or event begins (변화의 시발점) It is used for the place where a bus or subway starts, and for the trigger that began a bigger event. '출발점' is used more broadly, while 시발점 is often heard for the start of a route or the cause that set something off. Its opposite is '종점' (terminus).

examples.en: The main purpose of this trip is to rest.
What is the main purpose of this meeting?

examples.ko: 돈 버는 것이 제 주목적은 아니에요.
examples.en: Making money is not my main goal.
Don't forget the main objective when you make the plan.

examples.ko: 주목적과 부수적인 목적을 나눠서 적어 보세요.
examples.en: Try writing down the main objective separately from the side objectives.
My main reason for coming to Korea is to study abroad.

explain: '목적' 앞에 '주'가 붙어서 여러 목적 중 가장 중요한 것을 가리켜요. '주목적은 ~예요'처럼 문장 속에서 쓰이고, 짝이 되는 말로는 '부수적인 목적'이 있어요.

phrases.example: 이 책을 읽는 주된 목적은 공부예요.
phrases.en: The main purpose of reading this book is studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주목적'을 풀어 쓴 말이라 조금 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out version of 'jumokjeok' that sounds a bit softer.

phrases.example: 가장 큰 목적은 새 친구를 사귀는 거예요.
phrases.en: My biggest goal is to make new friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy phrase for everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 저는 한국어 공부를 주목적으로 한국에 왔어요.
phrases.en: I came to Korea mainly to study Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으로'를 붙이면 무엇을 위해 왔는지 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-으로', you can say what you came for.

explain_en: With '주' in front of '목적', it points to the most important among several purposes. It is used in sentences like '주목적은 ~예요', and its counterpart is '부수적인 목적' (a side purpose).

examples.en: I filled in my date of birth and place of birth on my résumé.
My place of birth and where I live now are different.
My birthplace is the seaside city of Busan.
They asked me where my place of birth is.
I moved around a lot from my place of birth.
Relatives still live in the village where I was born.

explain: 태어난 곳을 말하고, 서류나 소개 글에서 주로 써요. '고향'은 자란 곳이나 마음의 고향까지 포함해서 출생지와 다를 수 있어요. 말로는 '어디에서 태어났어요?'라고 물어요.

phrases.en: Please write your place of birth on the form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류를 쓸 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when filling out documents.
phrases.en_equiv: to write one's place of birth

phrases.en: My husband and I were born in different places.
phrases.nuance_ko: 태어난 곳을 서로 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing where people were born.

phrases.en: The place I was born is Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출생지를 말로 할 때 쓰는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, spoken way to say 출생지.

explain_en: Place where a person was born; forms, documents. It means the place where you were born and is mainly used on forms and in introductions. '고향' can include where you grew up or feel at home, so it may differ from 출생지. In speech, you'd ask '어디에서 태어났어요?'.

examples.en: At graduation we buried a time capsule in the ground.

examples.ko: 십 년 뒤에 타임캡슐을 열기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to open the time capsule ten years later.
I put letters and photos in the time capsule.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 타임캡슐에 무엇을 넣을지 정했어요.
examples.en: Our class decided what to put in the time capsule.
I forgot where the time capsule is buried.

examples.ko: 이 앨범은 타임캡슐처럼 옛날 모습을 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This album holds old memories like a time capsule.

explain: 먼 훗날 열어 보려고 물건을 넣어 묻어 두는 통을 말해요. '묻다', '열다', '넣다'와 같이 자주 쓰여요. 학교나 모임에서 기념으로 하는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: My friends and I buried a time capsule in the school playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 타임캡슐을 만들어 땅에 넣을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for burying a time capsule.

phrases.example: 십 년 뒤에 같이 타임캡슐을 열어 볼 거예요.
phrases.en: We will open the time capsule together in ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속한 날이 되어 꺼내 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the agreed day comes and you take it out.

phrases.example: 미래의 나에게 쓴 편지를 타임캡슐에 넣었어요.
phrases.en: I put a letter to my future self in the time capsule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 담았는지 말할 때 '에 넣다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '에 넣다' to say what you put inside.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in a time capsule

explain_en: This is a container filled with items and buried to be opened in the distant future. It often goes with '묻다' (bury), '열다' (open) and '넣다' (put in). Schools and groups often make one as a keepsake.

examples.en: Spinach contains a lot of iron.
This product contains natural ingredients.
I eat fruit containing vitamins every day.
I picked a snack that has no artificial colouring.

examples.ko: 이 물은 미네랄을 함유해서 맛이 부드러워요.
examples.en: This water contains minerals, so it tastes smooth.
The more sugar something contains, the higher its calories.

explain: 함유하다는 안에 어떤 성분을 가지고 있다는 뜻의 글말이에요. 말할 때는 '들어 있다'를 쓰고, 설명서나 광고, 뉴스에서 함유하다를 많이 봐요. '포함하다'는 여러 항목 중 하나로 넣는 것이고, 함유하다는 물질이 성분으로 들어 있을 때 써요.

phrases.en: Vitamins are contained in this tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성분이 안에 있다는 상태를 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive form describing the state of an ingredient being inside.

phrases.en: I often eat foods that contain iron.
phrases.nuance_ko: '함유한' 뒤에 식품이나 제품을 붙여 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a food or product after 함유한 to describe it.

phrases.example: 이 우유에는 칼슘이 많이 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: This milk has a lot of calcium in it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 함유하다 대신 쓰는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy spoken replacement for 함유하다.

explain_en: Hamyuhada is a written-style verb meaning something holds a substance as an ingredient. In speech people say 들어 있다, while manuals, ads, and news use 함유하다. 포함하다 is counting something as one item in a group, whereas 함유하다 is for a substance present as a component.

en: to grin to oneself; to smirk

examples.en: Why have you been grinning to yourself over and over since earlier?

examples.ko: 친구가 휴대폰을 보며 계속 히죽거리고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend keeps grinning while looking at the phone.
Stop smirking and tell me the reason.
My younger brother grinned when he saw his test score.
Even when he was teased, he just grinned and let it pass.
The way he was smirking was a bit annoying.

explain: 혼자 흐뭇해서, 또는 능글맞게 자꾸 웃는 모습이에요. 기분 좋은 일이 있을 때도 쓰지만 상대에게 쓰면 '실실 웃는다'는 비꼬는 느낌이 날 수 있어요. '히죽대다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: My friend keeps grinning next to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '히죽거리다'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 조금 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '히죽거리다' and a bit more casual in speech.

phrases.en: Please don't grin during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 실실 웃는 모습을 말릴 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to tell someone to stop smirking.

phrases.en: He walked off grinning to himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃는 행동과 다른 행동을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe grinning while doing something else.

explain_en: It describes smiling repeatedly, either from private satisfaction or in a sly way. It can be used for happy moments, but said about someone else it can sound like a mocking 'smirking around'. It can also be said as '히죽대다'.

t90.ax: Stop smirking and tell me the reason.

examples.en: He is all smooth talk and his actions don't follow.
His face was shiny and greasy because of the oil.
I wore shoes with a glossy shine.
He is a person who is only shiny on the surface.

examples.ko: 번지르르 말은 잘하는데 믿음이 안 가요.
examples.en: He talks smoothly, but I don't trust him.

examples.ko: 손에 로션을 발랐더니 번지르르 윤이 났어요.
examples.en: After I put lotion on my hands, they became glossy.

explain: 반들반들 윤이 나는 모습을 말하지만, 실제로는 '겉만 번지르르하다', '말만 번지르르하다'처럼 겉이나 말만 그럴듯하고 속은 부족하다는 부정적인 뉘앙스로 많이 써요. 보통 '번지르르하다/번지르르한' 형태로 써요.

phrases.example: 이 가게는 겉만 번지르르하고 음식 맛은 별로예요.
phrases.en: This restaurant only looks good on the outside, and the food is not great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 말은 그럴듯한데 알맹이는 부족할 때 비판하는 말투로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically when the appearance or words sound impressive but the substance is lacking.

explain_en: It describes a smooth, shiny look, but in practice it is often used negatively, as in '겉만 번지르르하다' or '말만 번지르르하다', meaning it only looks or sounds good on the outside. It is usually used in the forms '번지르르하다' or '번지르르한'.

t90.ax: I wore shoes with a glossy shine.

en: to be bustling; to be fussy; to be hectic

examples.en: The market is bustling from morning with merchants.
Guests came, so the kitchen was in a flurry for a while.
The meeting began in a hectic atmosphere.
The station will be bustling because the holiday is near.

examples.ko: 부산하게 짐을 싸는 모습이 눈에 띄었어요.
examples.en: The hurried way they packed stood out.

examples.ko: 사무실이 부산하지 않아서 일이 잘 돼요.
examples.en: The office isn't hectic, so work goes well.

explain: 도시 이름 '부산'과 소리가 같지만 다른 말이에요. '바쁘다'는 할 일이 많은 것이고, '부산하다'는 움직이는 모습이 어수선하고 서두르는 것이에요. '부산스럽다'와 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.example: 저녁이 되면 부산한 거리에 사람이 많아져요.
phrases.en: In the evening the bustling street gets crowded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요. 사람들이 바쁘게 오가는 장소에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, which fits places where people come and go busily.

phrases.en: On holiday mornings the family moves around busily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게' 형태로 동사를 꾸밀 수 있어요. 서두르고 어수선한 움직임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-게' form modifies a verb, describing hurried and restless movement.

phrases.en: The kids are so restless that I can't think straight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 사람이나 아이의 모습에 조금 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning; used a little more often for people or children.

explain_en: Busy with movement and noise; places like markets or streets. It sounds like the city name '부산' but is a different word. '바쁘다' means having a lot to do, while '부산하다' describes the hurried, disorderly look of people moving around. It is used much like '부산스럽다'.

dis.h: busy and hectic with movement and noise
gh: restless and fussy, making a stir

p.n: 부산스럽다 leans toward fussy, restless behavior.

t90.ax: The hurried way they packed stood out.

en: to be savage; to be bloody

examples.en: It's exam season, so the atmosphere in the library is tense and grim.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이가 살벌해서 말을 못 걸었어요.
examples.en: The mood between the two was so hostile that I couldn't talk to them.
Prices have risen brutally these days.
He stared at me with a fierce look, and I was scared.
The mood in the meeting was really harsh.
I heard the rent in this neighborhood is brutal.

explain: 분위기, 눈빛, 말투가 차갑고 적대적이라 긴장될 때 써요. '무섭다'와 달리 서로 맞서는 긴장감이 있고, 말할 때는 '살벌하게 비싸다'처럼 강조하는 말로도 써요.

phrases.example: 회의실이 살벌한 분위기여서 아무도 말을 못 했어요.
phrases.en: The meeting room had such a tense atmosphere that nobody could speak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차갑고 긴장돼서 숨쉬기 어려운 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a cold, tense atmosphere that is hard to breathe in.

phrases.example: 그 사람이 살벌한 눈빛으로 저를 쳐다봤어요.
phrases.en: That person stared at me with a menacing look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화가 나서 적대적으로 보는 눈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes eyes that look angry and hostile.

phrases.en: House prices in this neighborhood are brutally expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '아주 심하게'라는 뜻으로 강조하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, an intensifier meaning 'extremely'.

explain_en: It describes an atmosphere, look or tone that is cold and hostile, creating tension. Unlike '무섭다', it carries a sense of confrontation, and in speech it can also be an intensifier, as in '살벌하게 비싸다'.

en: to be unfailing; to be without fail

examples.ko: 월급날이면 어김없이 은행 앱에서 알림이 와요.
examples.en: On payday, a notification always arrives from my banking app.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 시간 약속이 어김없는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is someone who never fails to keep a time appointment.
His calculations are always spot on.
When spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom without fail.
It's an undeniable fact, so you can trust it.
I hate Mondays that come around without fail.

explain: 대부분 '어김없이'로 써요. '꼭', '틀림없이'와 비슷한데, '때가 되면 늘 그대로 반복된다'는 느낌이 강해요. 봄이 오는 것이나 월급날처럼 정해진 일에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: When autumn came, the leaves changed color without fail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어의 부사형이고 실제로 가장 많이 써요. 때가 되면 늘 그대로 일어난다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the adverb form and by far the most common one. It gives the feeling that something happens just as expected when the time comes.

phrases.en: He keeps his promises without fail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속이나 규칙을 한 번도 빼먹지 않고 지킨다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means keeping a promise or rule every time without missing once.

phrases.en: It will surely rain tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어김없이'와 비슷하지만, 반복되는 느낌보다 확실하다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 어김없이, but it stresses certainty more than repetition.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '어김없이'. It resembles '꼭' and '틀림없이', but carries a stronger sense that something repeats as expected whenever its time comes. It fits fixed events, like the arrival of spring or payday.

examples.ko: 다른 사람과 비교하면 내가 열등하다고 느껴질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: When I compare myself with others, sometimes I feel inferior.

examples.ko: 어떤 문화가 우월하거나 열등한 것은 아니에요.
examples.en: No culture is superior or inferior.

examples.ko: 남보다 열등해 보일까 봐 발표하기가 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried about presenting because I might look inferior to others.

examples.ko: 성적만으로 사람을 열등하게 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't look down on a person as inferior based only on grades.

examples.ko: 제 실력이 다른 선수보다 열등해서 속상했어요.
examples.en: I was upset because my skill was inferior to the other player's.

examples.ko: 자신이 열등하지 않다는 걸 증명하고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I wanted to prove that I'm not inferior.

explain: '못하다'보다 무겁고 강한 말이라서 사람에게 쓰면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있어요. 반대말은 '우월하다'이고, 일상에서는 '열등감'이라는 말을 더 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 친구와 비교하면 열등감이 들 때가 있어요.
phrases.en: Sometimes I feel inferior when I compare myself with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '열등하다'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life this is used more often than 열등하다 itself.

phrases.example: 다른 사람과 비교하면 제 실력이 열등해 보여요.
phrases.en: Compared with other people, my skills look inferior.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보이다'를 붙이면 겉으로 그렇게 보인다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 보이다 gives the sense that it merely looks that way.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 다른 팀보다 열등하지 않아요.
phrases.en: Our team is not inferior to the other teams.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 '못하지 않다'는 뜻을 강하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form firmly says 'not any worse'.

explain_en: It is heavier and stronger than '못하다' (to be poor at), so it can sound hurtful when applied to a person. The opposite is '우월하다' (superior), and in daily life people use '열등감' (inferiority complex) more often.
